page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.d1.3xlarge is a storage-focused virtual machine instance within the ecs.d1 family, running on the KVM hypervisor. It features 12 dedicated vCPUs powered by an Intel Xeon E5-2682v4 processor operating at 2.5 GHz on the x86_64 architecture. The hardware configuration includes 48.0 GB of system memory, providing a balanced 4.0 GB of RAM per core. A defining characteristic of this instance is its massive bundled local storage, consisting of 35,433 GB of HDD capacity. Network connectivity is supported by a baseline bandwidth of 4 Gbps.

Benchmark data reveals distinct performance tradeoffs. The single-core processing capabilities are limited, with stress-ng single-core performance and single-threaded bzip3 decompression scoring in the weak and poor categories respectively. However, multi-core execution is more robust, with stress-ng multi-core performance, Passmark CPU score, and multi-threaded bzip3 decompression all achieving average ratings. Memory performance is mixed; while cached and uncached memory bandwidth tests show average throughput, the Passmark memory score falls into the weak category. Static web serving throughput is also weak, reflecting the limitations of the underlying HDD storage for random read operations compared to modern SSDs.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the ecs.d1.3xlarge offers a high density of local storage capacity per resource unit, making it highly economical for workloads that require massive sequential data storage without the premium cost of solid-state drives. This profile is highly suitable for big data processing frameworks such as Apache Hadoop or Spark, large-scale log archiving, data warehousing, and sequential data analytics. It is less suited for high-IOPS databases or latency-sensitive web applications due to the performance characteristics of its HDD storage and weak single-core CPU metrics.
description: Alibaba Cloud ecs.d1.3xlarge is a storage-focused instance featuring 12 dedicated Intel Xeon E5-2682v4 vCPUs running at 2.5 GHz, 48.0 GB of RAM, and a substantial 35,433 GB of local HDD storage. Operating on the KVM hypervisor with a 4 Gbps baseline network bandwidth, this instance is designed for high-capacity sequential data workloads. Benchmark results indicate weak single-core CPU and memory performance, but average multi-core CPU and database operation capabilities. The massive local HDD capacity provides excellent qualitative cost efficiency for bulk storage, though it presents a tradeoff in random I/O speed compared to SSD-based instances. The ecs.d1.3xlarge is best suited for big data analytics, distributed file systems, log processing, and data archiving workloads that prioritize storage volume over high-speed random access.
